note: Floors are per split, in execution accuracy percent, taken as the minimum observed across the recent runs on Mini-Dev (G 9120c2b, H d5927b0, I 700529b, J 4ad0181, 1.0.0 run 39762058351, and the 13-arm runs since), applied to the full 500-question split. A rerun may land below a floor by tolerancePp before the gate fails, because ADR-166 measured that anything inside 4pp cannot be separated from sampling noise at n=239. `inline+retrieval`, `inline+icl`, `inline+repair`, `inline+repair-raw`, `select`, `select5` and `values` were added to the chain after those runs and have no floors yet: the gate records their first measurement and says so rather than inventing a threshold. A run scored on fewer than 95% of the baseline sample fails as a changed sample. `armsBySplit` states which arms each split runs; the dev split compares against a published leaderboard, needs five arms rather than thirteen, and now carries floors of its own taken from the two runs of `40202780469` and `40245630669` — the split that decides adoption is the split that must also guard against regression. A floor is a claim about three coordinates — split, arms, and model — and the model was the one missing: `bird-model.yml` therefore skipped this tool entirely for cross-model runs, which also skipped the funnel, cost and empty-lever checks. `floorModel` states the model each floor was taken on, and a run by another model is measured rather than failed while every structural check still applies. `scoredBySplit` does the same for the sample size: the dev split was being compared against Mini-Dev's 500, so a dev run scoring 600 of 1,532 questions passed a check whose whole job is to notice a shrunken sample. A floor is also a claim about which second model wrote the cross candidates: `select-cross` draws one of its three prompts from a second model, so its dev floor (61.7, run 40806666847) is recorded in `floorSecondModel.dev` and a run that used another second model is measured rather than failed — the same treatment `floorModel` gives the primary model. The arm is listed in `armsBySplit.dev` even though routine dev runs do not request it, because a floor that no arm list mentions is a floor nothing will notice.
